views.reconstructed_statement: For every nonnegative integer degree d, every infinite real coefficient sequence c, and every real u,v,lo,hi, assume 0<=u<v<=1 and lo<=c(r)<=hi for each integer r with 0<=r<=d. Then for every integer i with 0<=i<=d, the coefficient R(i) obtained by the following two subdivisions lies in the same closed interval [lo,hi]. Write D_t(c)(j)=(1-t)c(j)+t c(j+1); casteljau(m,c,t,j) means D_t iterated m times and evaluated at j. Set L_t(c)(i)=D_t^i(c)(0), set Q(i)=L_(1-u)(r -> c(d-r))(d-i), using natural subtraction max(d-i,0), and set R(i)=L_s(Q)(i), where s=(v-u)/(1-u). These are exact real equalities, with no rounding or tolerance. Equivalently Q(i)=sum over j=0,...,max(d-i,0) of c(d-j) B(max(d-i,0),j,1-u); for i<=d all accessed original indices are between i and d. For i>d, Q(i)=c(d), explaining why the supplied right-restriction node legitimately quantifies over all natural i. The root itself quantifies only over i<=d. The assumptions imply u<1, so the denominator 1-u is strictly positive and s belongs to (0,1]. The asserted range preservation is a closed-interval coefficient bound, not a statement about normalized quantum amplitudes.

domains_and_quantifiers.c: all functions Nat -> Real; no finite-support requirement

hypotheses: for every natural r<=d, lo<=c(r) and c(r)<=hi
semantic_slots.closed_interval_meaning: membership in Set.Icc lo hi means the conjunction lo<=value and value<=hi
semantic_slots.basis: B(d,r,t)=binomial(d,r)t^r(1-t)^(d-r), with natural subtraction and binomial(d,r)=0 when r>d; only r<=d occurs in the finite sums used here
semantic_slots.normalization: Bernstein weights sum to one for every real t; they are nonnegative on [0,1]. This is affine weight normalization only.
boundary_cases: d=0: the sole admitted coefficient and the output R(0) both equal c(0).
u=0 and v=1 are admitted jointly; u=v and u=1 are excluded.
v=1 gives s=1 and remains admitted.
No lo<=hi premise is written separately. The coefficient premise implies it through c(0); if lo>hi the implication has no satisfying coefficient premise.
There is no empty degree-d coefficient range: it always contains index zero. Coefficients beyond d have no effect on the claimed output indices.

obligation_nodes.meaning: For every d>=0 and every real t, sum_(r=0)^d B(d,r,t)=1; no restriction t in [0,1] is needed for this identity.
For every d,c,t,lo,hi, if 0<=t<=1 and all first d+1 coefficients lie in [lo,hi], their Bernstein-weighted sum lies in [lo,hi]. Both premises are required.
For every d,c,u,lo,hi, if 0<=u<=1 and all first d+1 coefficients lie in [lo,hi], then Q(i) lies there for every natural i, including i>d via truncated subtraction.
For all real u,v satisfying all three inequalities 0<=u, u<v, v<=1, the exact-real quotient (v-u)/(1-u) belongs to [0,1].
Under every original premise, all admitted restricted coefficients belong to the same interval.

views.reconstructed_statement: For every pair of types alpha,beta (with arbitrary row type alpha and a finite, possibly empty column type beta), every natural k,M, every real a,h with h>0, and every pair of functions u:alpha->Nat and v:beta->Nat satisfying v(y)<M for every y, form the real matrix F(x,y)=f_k(a+h n(x,y)), where n(x,y)=M u(x)+v(y) is computed in Nat and then cast to Real. The datum is f_k(p)=exp(p) for p<-1, the specified Hermite bridge polynomial P_k(p) for -1<=p<=0, and exp(-p) for p>0. The packet characterizes P_k as degree at most 2k+1 with bridge value P_k(0)=1 and matching endpoint jets. The root asserts the conjunction of three conclusions: (1) there exist real matrices A:alpha x I_k and B:I_k x beta such that, for every x,y, F(x,y)=sum_(z in I_k) A(x,z)B(z,y); (2) the finite intermediate type I_k=(((Fin 2 x Unit) disjoint-union ((Fin 2 disjoint-union Fin 2) x Fin(2k+2))) disjoint-union (Fin 2 x Unit)) has exactly 8k+12 elements; and (3) the real algebraic rank of F is at most 8k+12. Both factor witnesses are part of the existential conclusion; no witness is an extra input assumption. No finite-row, injectivity, monotonicity, or distinct-sample hypothesis is present.

semantic_slots.factorization_and_rank: F=A*B is finite-width exact real matrix multiplication, i.e. a finite sum through I_k; rank is the supplied real algebraic matrix rank, bounded without requiring a finite row set.
all_root_conjuncts: Existence of both factor matrices through the specified finite type
Exact cardinality of that intermediate type
Rank upper bound for the same sampled matrix
boundary_cases: k=0 is admitted and yields width 12; no positive-k premise is available.

M=0 is not globally excluded. If beta is inhabited the condition v(y)<M forces M>0. If beta is empty the condition is vacuous even at M=0, the matrix has no columns, its rank is zero, and the factorization is vacuous on entries.
An empty alpha is also admitted and gives an empty row matrix.
h=0 and negative h are excluded; a is unrestricted.
At p=-1 the polynomial branch is selected; at p=0 it is also selected. The supplied value P_k(0)=1 makes replacement by the right exponential at that one boundary legitimate.
Natural ceiling used by a possible threshold construction saturates negative inputs to zero; it is not an integer ceiling taking negative values.

obligation_nodes.meaning: For all natural M,x,y,T with y<M, M*x+y<T iff x<T div M or (x=T div M and y<T mod M). At M=0 the premise cannot hold for any natural y.

For arbitrary row/column types and functions with v(y)<M, both the threshold indicator matrix 1_[M*u(x)+v(y)<T] and its pointwise complement factor through Fin 2. The conclusion is an AND of two factorization existences.
Under h>0 AND the column-digit bound, the particular three-branch exponential-polynomial-exponential sample matrix has an I_k factorization.
For every k, the exact cardinality of I_k is 8*k+12.
The same assumptions entail the factorization AND exact bond cardinality AND rank upper bound.

provided_auxiliary_interfaces: A degree-at-most-d polynomial evaluated at row-real plus column-real admits a factorization through Fin(d+1).
The exponential of a row-real plus column-real admits a factorization through Unit.

The root rank conclusion needs the general principle that an F=A*B factorization through a finite I bounds rank by |I|, in addition to the displayed factorization and cardinality nodes. Merely counting a type unrelated to a factorization cannot bound matrix rank.
